title_en: US releases files on suspected Bigfoot sightings in Montana and Oregon
title_zh: 美国公布蒙大拿州和俄勒冈州疑似大脚怪目击事件的文件
summary: Forest Service releases files months after residents in rural Ontario reported encounters with massive figures Bigfoot has quietly appeared again. Well, not Sasquatch directly, but new files about the cryptid. “The stride of the tracks did not change with slop
summary_zh: 安大略省农村居民报告遭遇大脚怪再次悄然出现的几个月后，林务局发布了文件。威尔
body_en: Forest Service releases files months after residents in rural Ontario reported encounters with massive figures
Well, not Sasquatch directly, but new files about the cryptid.
In a public archive, the US Forest Service recently added reports concerning suspected encounters with Bigfoot – or its remnants in Montana and Oregon.
A newly released 1982 report showed how a wildlife biologist investigated peculiar tracks in north-east Oregon.

The additional documents also included a 2003 Montana newspaper story about a reported sighting of Bigfoot tracks and a testimonial about the history of a creek area in Montana where people spotted what they thought was “a very large bear, except bears don’t walk on their hind legs only for short distances”.
The recent release of the files by the US Forest Service comes months after residents in rural Ontario, Canada, reported encounters with massive figures that matched the description of Bigfoot.

Collectively, they add to a long history of suspected sightings of Bigfoot or markings from the bipedal ape whose existence has not been confirmed by science. The Bigfoot Mapping Project contains more than 16,000 reports on the cryptid, a term referring to an animal or creature whose existence has not been proven.
Carleton University philosophy professor Josh Redstone previously told the Guardian that Bigfoot is a prime example of how fascinating the unverified can be for humans.
“For people who believe in Sasquatch, there’s an excitement around the possibility of discovering something new,” Redstone said.

In the 1982 report, the biologist, Rodney Johnson, investigated tracks at three locations in the Umatilla National Forest in north-east Oregon . To determine their origin, Johnson – or a fellow investigator – made plaster casts of two of the tracks.
Johnson gave eight reasons why he did not think the tracks belonged to Sasquatch, including
“The stride of the tracks did not change with slope.”
“The tracks at both sites were not to the ‘bottom’ of the mud.
“The small toes lack a definite ‘pad’ at the tips as would be expected.”
Still, Johnson did not entirely dismiss the Bigfoot theory.

“If the tracks were faked, someone went to a great deal of trouble and detail,” Johnson wrote. “The ‘print’ marks on the foot would have to be very hard to duplicate. They appear very natural. I would almost suspect a cast made of an actual foot would have had to be used to make the ‘fake’ feet. If this were the case though, the other creases in the foot should have shown.”
In a subsequent report from the forest service, the investigator stated that the tracks “were a very clever attempt to perpetrate a hoax”.
“Trusting that this memo will suffice to close this ‘Bigfoot’ case,” the report stated.
body_zh: 安大略省农村居民报告遭遇大规模人物数月后，林务局发布了文件
好吧，不是直接 Sasquatch，而是关于 cryptid 的新文件。
美国林务局最近在公共档案中添加了有关疑似在蒙大拿州和俄勒冈州遭遇大脚怪或其残余物的报告。
1982 年新发布的一份报告展示了一位野生动物生物学家如何调查俄勒冈州东北部的奇特足迹。
其他文件还包括 2003 年蒙大拿州报纸的一篇报道，内容是关于目击大脚足迹的报道，以及一份关于蒙大拿州小溪地区历史的证言，人们在那里发现了他们认为的“一只非常大的熊，只不过熊不仅仅用后腿行走短距离”。
美国林务局最近公布这些文件的几个月前，加拿大安大略省农村地区的居民报告称遇到了与大脚怪描述相符的巨大人物。
总的来说，它们增加了疑似目击大脚怪或双足猿标记的悠久历史，但其存在尚未得到科学证实。大脚怪测绘项目包含超过 16,000 份有关神秘生物的报告，这个术语指的是尚未证实其存在的动物或生物。
卡尔顿大学哲学教授乔什·雷石东此前告诉《卫报》，大脚怪是一个很好的例子，说明未经证实的事物对人类来说是多么着迷。
“对于相信大脚野人的人来说，发现新事物的可能性令人兴奋，”雷石东说。
在 1982 年的报告中，生物学家罗德尼·约翰逊 (Rodney Johnson) 对俄勒冈州东北部尤马蒂拉国家森林中三个地点的足迹进行了调查。为了确定它们的起源，约翰逊或一位调查员同事对其中两条足迹进行了石膏模型。
约翰逊给出了他认为这些足迹不属于大脚野人的八个理由，包括
“轨道的步幅不随坡度变化。”
“两个地点的铁轨都没有到达泥浆的‘底部’。
“正如预期的那样，小脚趾的尖端缺乏明确的‘垫’。”
尽管如此，约翰逊并没有完全驳回大脚怪理论。
约翰逊写道：“如果这些踪迹是伪造的，就会有人花费大量的精力和细节。” “脚上的‘印刷’痕迹很难复制。它们看起来非常自然。我几乎怀疑必须用真脚制成的模型来制作‘假’脚。但如果是这样的话，脚上的其他折痕应该会显示出来。”
在林务局随后的一份报告中，调查人员表示，这些痕迹“是一次非常聪明的骗局”。
报告称：“相信这份备忘录足以结束这起‘大脚怪’案。”

title_en: Army plans to carry out detonation at Iowa plant on Wednesday
title_zh: 陆军计划周三在爱荷华州工厂进行爆炸
summary: The Department of the Army said it plans to use an emergency munitions and explosives exclusion to the Environmental Protection Agency's permit.
summary_zh: 美国陆军部表示，计划使用紧急弹药和爆炸物，但须获得环境保护局的许可。
body_en: U.S. Army plans to carry out detonation at Iowa plant on Wednesday despite indefinite pause - CBS News

The U.S. Army says it plans to move forward with the detonation of several tons of unstable explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday "to allow for optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced," the military said in a post on social media Sunday night.
The Army had earlier said in a court filing that it planned to carry out the detonation by Tuesday.

The detonation is being planned despite a federal court order that paused it indefinitely, which the Army said it does not need to follow because of the public safety risks associated with the possibility of the explosives detonating on their own.

In federal court records filed late Saturday, the Department of the Army said it plans to use an emergency munitions and explosives exclusion to the Environmental Protection Agency's permit. The government argues it needs to perform a controlled detonation to protect the public from the more significant threat from an uncontrolled explosion.

On Friday, a federal court suspended the U.S. Army's plan to detonate the explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Middletown, Iowa, after community outcry about the risk of toxic lead particles spreading in a dust plume across parts of Iowa and Illinois.
The Army originally scheduled two controlled explosions for Friday. The Army then delayed them until Monday before the court stepped in.
The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals granted an emergency motion to pause the demolition after environmental groups filed a lawsuit.
Why the Army says it needs to detonate unstable, lead-filled explosives in Iowa and what's at risk
The military said on Friday it was working closely with the Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA to ensure the controlled explosion would be conducted in the safest manner possible.

"Officials have been meticulously planning for this event since March, and all agencies involved are prepared to take the most extreme mitigation measures available to ensure there is no risk to the public and any disruptions are minimized," the statement said.

In its filing on Saturday, the government had warned that it must conduct the controlled explosion by Tuesday because the temperature is expected to drop below 30 degrees in the next several days. It says the lead azide has deteriorated and that crystals in the waste could break as temperatures drop. It did not immediately explain if the forecast or other factors had changed to make a move to Wednesday safer.

"A controlled detonation allows the Army to implement measures to minimize the risk to the public, including the risk from the ejection of partial unexploded ordnances that can explode later from the Facility," the court filing says. "The Army intends to act consistent with the terms of the Emergency Permit and its mitigation measures even if not in effect. That includes mitigation measures to minimize the risk of the dispersal of lead dust. In short, a controlled detonation is by far safer than an uncontrolled explosion."
In response to the Army's filing, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club filed a motion Sunday seeking to supplement their emergency request to block the planned detonation.

The filing includes three expert and local government declarations challenging the Army's assessment of the risk of delaying the detonation, as well as concerns about public notice and potential health and environmental impacts.

In a statement Sunday, the Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice questioned claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration, saying "this emergency is of the Army's own making."

"The Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public's demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm," said Earthjustice Attorney Thien Chau.

Iowa's new Democratic Senator-elect Josh Turek said in a statement Sunday that he is "concerned about the potential health risks resulting from the U.S. Army's planned detonation in Middletown and the lack of clear communication and transparency from the U.S. Army."

"I also believe we need a full investigation into why this stockpile of lead azide, which has been at IAAAP for decades, was allowed to degrade into this critical state, why safer methods of disposal were not pursued, what other potentially dangerous materials are being stored at the IAAAP and their condition, and what procedures are needed to ensure this never happens again," he said. "The public also deserves answers as to why the U.S. Army's communication — both with the public and with Iowa officials — was delayed and inadequate from the beginning."

In March of this year, the Army said it discovered that 68 drums of lead azide at the site had started "recrystallization." The lead was stored in bunkers at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, a munitions plant built in 1941, which produces quality medium- and large-caliber munitions.
body_zh: 尽管无限期暂停，美国陆军仍计划周三在爱荷华州工厂进行爆炸 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
美国陆军周日晚上在社交媒体上发帖称，计划周三在爱荷华州一家军工厂引爆数吨不稳定炸药，“以实现最佳天气条件并采取所有缓解措施”。
陆军早些时候在一份法庭文件中表示，计划在周二之前进行爆炸。
尽管联邦法院命令无限期暂停爆炸，但爆炸仍在计划中，陆军表示不需要遵循该命令，因为炸药可能自行爆炸会带来公共安全风险。
在周六晚间提交的联邦法院记录中，陆军部表示，计划在环境保护局的许可下使用紧急弹药和爆炸物。政府认为需要进行受控爆炸，以保护公众免受失控爆炸带来的更重大威胁。
周五，联邦法院暂停了美国陆军在爱荷华州米德尔敦一家军工厂引爆含有叠氮化铅的炸药的计划，此前社区对有毒铅颗粒在爱荷华州和伊利诺伊州部分地区的尘埃羽流中传播的风险表示强烈抗议。
陆军原定于周五进行两次受控爆炸。陆军随后将他们推迟到周一，法院才介入。
在环保组织提起诉讼后，美国第八巡回上诉法院批准了暂停拆除行动的紧急动议。
为什么陆军表示需要在爱荷华州引爆不稳定的含铅炸药以及存在哪些风险
军方周五表示，正在与卫生与公众服务部和美国环保署密切合作，以确保以尽可能安全的方式进行受控爆炸。
声明称：“自三月份以来，官员们一直在精心策划这次活动，所有相关机构都准备采取最极端的缓解措施，以确保公众不会面临风险，并将任何干扰降至最低。”
政府在周六提交的文件中警告说，必须在周二之前进行受控爆炸，因为预计未来几天气温将降至 30 度以下。据称，叠氮化铅已经变质，随着温度下降，废物中的晶体可能会破裂。它没有立即解释预测或其他因素是否发生变化，以使周三的比赛更加安全。
法庭文件称：“受控爆炸使陆军能够采取措施，尽量减少公众面临的风险，包括部分未爆炸弹药弹射后可能从设施中爆炸的风险。” “即使没有生效，陆军也打算按照紧急许可证的条款及其缓解措施采取行动。这包括最大限度地减少铅尘扩散风险的缓解措施。简而言之，受控爆炸比不受控制的爆炸安全得多。”
作为对陆军提交文件的回应，爱荷华州环境委员会和塞拉俱乐部周日提交了一项动议，寻求补充他们阻止计划中的爆炸的紧急请求。
该文件包括三份专家和地方政府的声明，质疑陆军对延迟爆炸风险的评估，以及对公众关注以及潜在的健康和环境影响的担忧。
在周日的一份声明中，爱荷华州环境委员会、塞拉俱乐部和地球正义组织对所有替代方案都得到适当考虑的说法提出质疑，称“这种紧急情况是陆军自己造成的”。
地球正义律师 Thien Chau 表示：“周末，陆军似乎更关心的是找到绕过司法程序的方法，而不是满足公众对提高透明度、通知受影响社区以及更有力保护人民、财产和环境免受严重伤害的要求。”
爱荷华州新任民主党参议员乔什·图雷克周日在一份声明中表示，他“对美国陆军计划在米德尔敦进行的爆炸以及美国陆军缺乏明确沟通和透明度造成的潜在健康风险感到担忧”。
他说：“我还认为，我们需要全面调查为什么IAAP中存放了数十年的叠氮化铅库存会退化到这种临界状态，为什么没有采取更安全的处置方法，IAAP中还存放着哪些其他潜在危险材料及其状况，以及需要采取哪些程序来确保这种情况不再发生。” “公众也应该得到答案，为什么美国陆军与公众和爱荷华州官员的沟通从一开始就被延迟和不充分。”
今年3月，陆军表示，发现现场68桶叠氮化铅已经开始“再结晶”。铅储存在爱荷华州陆军弹药厂的掩体中，该弹药厂建于 1941 年，生产优质中型和大口径弹药。

title_en: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
title_zh: 万斯没有支持特朗普关于伊朗接近拥有核武器的说法
summary: US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclea
summary_zh: 美国副总统在白宫新闻发布会上表示，他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但他没有支持特朗普的说法
body_en: US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim

At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic.

In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.

“I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said. “I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that if it were asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”

However, Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to developing a nuclear weapon this year that it was necessary to go to war, which he has made dozens of times in the past nine months, is undermined by public evidence and contradicts his own previous statements on US strikes against Iranian facilities in 2025.
At a campaign rally in Alaska last month, Trump insisted that he had to join Israel in attacking Iran in February because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”.

That claim appears at odds with what his then director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, testified to Congress on 25 March 2025, two months into Trump’s second term: that US intelligence agencies reported that Iran had not tried to make a nuclear weapon for more than two decades. The US intelligence community, Gabbard said, “continues to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and supreme leader Khamenei has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”.

Despite that assessment, three months later, on 21 June 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities. The strikes, Trump told the public that night , “were a spectacular military success. Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.”

Eight months after that, however, when Trump announced the start of a full-scale war on Iran early on 28 February 2026, he said in a video statement from Mar-a-Lago the war was necessary to “ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon”.
The morning after this month’s midterm elections, Vance said in a statement posted on social media: “The reason we lost is the war.”

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” he added. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost.”

In the White House briefing room on Friday, after Trump said that Vance should have said the war was necessary, a reporter asked the vice-president whether he would argue that the war in Iran was worth it.

In his response, Vance said it was not his place to second-guess the president, but refrained from actually endorsing Trump’s claim that the war was essential to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon.

“Look, what I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, of innocent people,” Vance said. “I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again.”
“My view is that my goal is, and my job is, to support the president of the United States,” the vice-president said.
The vice president’s office did not respond to a request to comment.
body_zh: 美国副总统表示他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但没有支持特朗普的说法
在周五的白宫新闻发布会上，JD 万斯没有支持唐纳德·特朗普的说法，即伊朗在二月份非常接近获得核武器，以至于美国必须与这个伊斯兰共和国开战。
在白宫简报室，特朗普被问及本周的报道，他对美国副总统将共和党在中期选举中的失败归咎于伊朗战争的声明感到不满。
“我没有说我对此不满意，”特朗普说。 “我认为这个声明很好，除了我还有另一件事，如果有人问我，我会说：‘你会再做一次吗？’绝对，答案是肯定的，因为我们不能允许伊朗拥有核武器。”
然而，特朗普声称伊朗今年已经非常接近研制出核武器，以至于有必要发动战争，而他在过去九个月里已经多次提出这一说法，这一说法被公开证据所推翻，并且与他之前关于美国将于2025年袭击伊朗设施的说法相矛盾。
上个月在阿拉斯加举行的竞选集会上，特朗普坚称他必须在二月份与以色列一起攻击伊朗，因为“他们距离拥有核武器还有两周时间”。
这一说法似乎与时任国家情报总监图尔西·加巴德 (Tulsi Gabbard) 于 2025 年 3 月 25 日（也就是特朗普第二任期两个月后）向国会作证时的说法不一致：美国情报机构报告称，伊朗已有二十多年没有尝试制造核武器。加巴德表示，美国情报界“继续评估伊朗没有制造核武器，最高领袖哈梅内伊也没有授权他在 2003 年暂停的核武器计划”。
尽管有这样的评估，三个月后，即 2025 年 6 月 21 日，特朗普还是下令美国轰炸伊朗的核浓缩设施。特朗普当晚告诉公众，这次袭击“在军事上取得了巨大的成功。伊朗的关键核浓缩设施已被彻底摧毁。”
然而八个月后，当特朗普于 2026 年 2 月 28 日早些时候宣布对伊朗发动全面战争时，他在海湖庄园的视频声明中表示，这场战争对于“确保伊朗不会获得核武器”是必要的。
本月中期选举后的第二天早上，万斯在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中表示：“我们失败的原因是战争。”
“如果你想说这是值得的，认为在未来六年失去参议院是值得的，那就这么做吧，”他补充道。 “认为这是值得付出的代价。无论同意还是不同意，这至少是诚实的。但每个人都知道我们为什么输了。”
周五在白宫新闻发布室，特朗普表示万斯应该表示这场战争是必要的，之后一名记者问副总统是否会认为伊朗战争值得。
万斯在回应中表示，他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但他没有真正支持特朗普的说法，即这场战争对于阻止伊朗制造核武器至关重要。
“听着，我所说的是，阻止伊朗获得核武器的目标绝对是我们需要做的。它是恐怖主义的最大支持者。如果他们拥有核武器，他们就会用它作为杠杆，否则，上帝保佑，他们会攻击并杀害数千、数十万无辜人民，”万斯说。 “我认为总统是做出决定的人，总统已经说过他会再次这样做。”
“我的观点是，我的目标是，我的工作是支持美国总统，”副总统说。
副总统办公室没有回应置评请求。

title_en: Experts say ‘trusted messengers’ critical as Amish grapple with measles outbreak
title_zh: 专家表示，阿米什人应对麻疹疫情时，“值得信赖的信使”至关重要
summary: Unfolding crisis shows importance of ‘human connections’ over the long term – especially in under-vaccinated areas Tristan Sharratt, a family nurse practitioner and public health researcher, began serving an Amish community in central New York almost inadverte
summary_zh: 正在展开的危机显示了长期“人际关系”的重要性——尤其是在疫苗接种不足的地区。
body_en: Unfolding crisis shows importance of ‘human connections’ over the long term – especially in under-vaccinated areas

T ristan Sharratt, a family nurse practitioner and public health researcher, began serving an Amish community in central New York almost inadvertently. A friend told an Amish neighbor that Sharratt was accepting new patients and was a good, solid guy. Word spread quickly, and now Sharratt sees many members of the community, which numbers in the hundreds.
US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991

He is what is called a “trusted messenger” – someone who understands a community and has earned their respect. Other trusted messengers can be neighbors, co-workers, customers, midwives, or people who work as long-distance drivers for the Amish. Connecting with such people will be crucial for ending the measles outbreak and preventing future crises.

“We can’t build trust with these communities just dropping in and being like, ‘Hey, there’s a measles outbreak. You should get vaccinated.’ Trust-building with these communities takes months to years,” Sharratt said. “This is a hard lesson and a tremendous opportunity to start building connections with these communities, because that is what it’s going to take to prevent the next situation like this.”

The unfolding measles outbreak, which has killed at least eight people in Pennsylvania, two in Wisconsin, one in New York, and one in Virginia, also demonstrates the importance of funding public health long-term – for everything from water fluoridation to road safety, said Sharratt, who is also a clinical lecturer of nursing and public health at Binghamton University.
“There’s just this enormous amount of work to be done,” he said.

Measles has raged through communities of Plain Anabaptists – including Amish and Mennonites – in this and previous outbreaks, and they are “emblematic” of many rural communities that have not been reached well by public health, Sharratt said.
“We haven’t invested in rural communities in a long time from a public health perspective,” Sharratt said, “and we’re really seeing the consequences with this outbreak.”

A central belief for the Amish is Gelassenheit, which essentially means “God’s will” – the idea that one’s life belongs to God; both joy and suffering are God’s will. “Part of my conversations with them is trying to determine why scientific advancements don’t fit into the perspective of God’s will,” Sharratt said. “Why is it not God’s will that scientists have developed the technology to [prevent measles]?”

Being unvaccinated in Plain Anabaptist communities is usually “an outcome of this whole idea of plain living”, Sharratt said. But the work of anti-vaccine activists accelerated alongside the Covid pandemic, and “unfortunately it has started to creep in” to Amish communities as well, Sharratt said. Non-Amish anti-vaccine groups such as Children’s Health Defense – then led by Robert F Kennedy Jr, now the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services – held events and wrote articles for Plain Anabaptist publications, overtly targeting the communities with vaccine misinformation.
Amish life centers around community, and so should efforts to reach them.

“Human connection really should be at the center,” Sharratt said. “You really just have to approach these people as people, build relationships as peers first, and then be there when they’re ready to talk to you or ask your opinion about these health issues.”

Inroads to Amish communities are frequently informal. “Maybe the associate public health director just happens to drive by the Amish farm every day and buy something from the vegetable stand – it can be as simple as that,” Sharratt said. Business owners and contractors can be a good way to connect.

“The Amish will work as subcontractors, and then all of a sudden you’re working next to Amos on the build site, and you’re there for eight hours together doing rough carpentry, and you have the chance to talk,” he said. “Maybe you go to an Amish family’s bake stand every Saturday to get the pie, and you just happen to run into them and build a relationship.”

There are local health departments that have done a great job of building connections – Sharratt pointed to the Otsego county health department, which developed a strong relationship with two Amish communities two decades ago during a pertussis outbreak; they continue to run vaccine clinics three to four times a year with those communities.
Often, however, health departments might know where a Plain Anabaptist community is, but they might not know how many people live there, how many children there are, or what the vaccination rate is.

“We have a huge data problem with these communities,” Sharratt said. “That requires going back to old methods of epidemiology, of community public health.” And public health at the national and state level hasn’t been as focused on community-building, he said.

Many Amish people want access to modern medicine when they need it – but access is frequently a challenge. Most Amish communities participate in some version of community insurance, where everyone chips in to cover healthcare costs. But typically providers accept conventional insurance; even those who negotiate lower prices with uninsured patients may be cost-prohibitive – especially as medicine is more corporatized and profit-driven, Sharratt said. That means communities often end up with providers who may not be as locked into conventional medicine.
body_zh: 正在展开的危机显示了长期“人际关系”的重要性——尤其是在疫苗接种不足的地区
特里斯坦·沙拉特 (Tristan Sharratt) 是一名家庭护士和公共卫生研究员，几乎无意中开始为纽约中部的阿米什社区提供服务。一位朋友告诉一位阿米什邻居，沙拉特正在接受新病人，他是一个善良、踏实的人。消息很快传开，现在沙拉特看到了社区的许多成员，人数达到数百人。
由于1991年以来最严重的麻疹疫情，美国失去了消除麻疹的地位
他是所谓的“值得信赖的使者”——了解社区并赢得社区尊重的人。其他值得信赖的信使可以是邻居、同事、客户、助产士或阿米什人的长途司机。与这些人建立联系对于结束麻疹疫情和预防未来危机至关重要。
“我们无法与这些社区建立信任，只是顺便拜访一下，然后说，‘嘿，麻疹爆发了。你应该接种疫苗。’与这些社区建立信任需要数月甚至数年的时间，”沙拉特说。 “这是一个惨痛的教训，也是一个开始与这些社区建立联系的巨大机会，因为只有这样才能防止下一次类似情况的发生。”
宾厄姆顿大学护理和公共卫生临床讲师沙拉特表示，正在蔓延的麻疹疫情已导致宾夕法尼亚州至少 8 人死亡、威斯康星州两人死亡、纽约州一人死亡、弗吉尼亚州一人死亡，这也表明了长期资助公共卫生的重要性——从饮水氟化到道路安全等各个方面。
“还有大量的工作要做，”他说。
沙拉特说，在这次和之前的疫情中，麻疹在包括阿米什人和门诺派在内的普通再洗礼派社区肆虐，他们是许多公共卫生尚未得到很好覆盖的农村社区的“象征”。
“从公共卫生的角度来看，我们已经很长时间没有对农村社区进行投资了，”沙拉特说，“我们确实看到了这次疫情爆发的后果。”
阿米什人的核心信仰是“Gelassenheit”，它本质上意味着“上帝的意志”——即一个人的生命属于上帝的观念；喜乐和苦难都是神的旨意。 “我与他们对话的一部分是试图确定为什么科学进步不符合上帝意志的观点，”沙拉特说。 “为什么科学家开发出[预防麻疹]技术不是上帝的旨意？”
沙拉特说，在普通再洗礼派社区中未接种疫苗通常是“整个朴素生活理念的结果”。但沙拉特说，随着新冠病毒大流行，反疫苗活动人士的工作也加速了，“不幸的是，它也开始蔓延”到阿米什社区。非阿米什人反疫苗团体，例如儿童健康保卫会（当时由现任美国卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪领导）举办活动，并为普通再洗礼派出版物撰写文章，公然针对社区发布疫苗错误信息。
阿米什人的生活以社区为中心，因此应该努力接触社区。
“人与人之间的联系确实应该处于中心地位，”沙拉特说。 “你真的只需要像人一样接近这些人，首先建立作为同伴的关系，然后当他们准备好与你交谈或询问你对这些健康问题的意见时就在那里。”
对阿米什社区的入侵往往是非正式的。沙拉特说：“也许公共卫生副主任只是碰巧每天开车路过阿米什农场，从蔬菜摊买点东西——事情就这么简单。”企业主和承包商可能是一种很好的联系方式。
“阿米什人将作为分包商，然后突然间你就在建筑工地上和阿莫斯一起工作，你们一起在那里做八个小时的粗木工，并且你们有机会交谈，”他说。 “也许你每个周六都会去阿米什家庭的面包店买馅饼，然后你恰好遇到他们并建立了关系。”
当地卫生部门在建立联系方面做得很好——沙拉特指出，奥齐戈县卫生部门在二十年前的百日咳爆发期间与两个阿米什社区建立了牢固的关系；他们继续每年与这些社区一起开设三到四次疫苗诊所。
然而，卫生部门通常可能知道普通再洗礼派社区在哪里，但他们可能不知道那里有多少人居住，有多少儿童，或者疫苗接种率是多少。
“我们在这些社区中遇到了巨大的数据问题，”沙拉特说。 “这需要回到流行病学和社区公共卫生的旧方法。”他说，国家和州一级的公共卫生并没有那么关注社区建设。
许多阿米什人希望在需要时获得现代医学，但获得现代医学往往是一个挑战。大多数阿米什社区都参加某种形式的社区保险，每个人都出钱支付医疗费用。但提供商通常接受传统保险；沙拉特说，即使是那些与未参保患者协商降低价格的人，成本也可能过高，尤其是在医药业更加公司化和利润驱动的情况下。这意味着社区最终往往会找到可能不那么局限于传统医学的医疗服务提供者。

title_en: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and sports broadcaster, dies at 75
title_zh: 前野马队球星兼体育广播员汤姆·杰克逊去世，享年 75 岁
summary: Tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and ESPN analyst, has died at 75.
summary_zh: 前丹佛野马队球员兼 ESPN 分析师汤姆·杰克逊 (Tom Jackson) 去世，享年 75 岁。
body_en: Former football star and famed broadcaster Tom Jackson has died, his family and ESPN announced Sunday.

Jackson rose to prominence as a Denver Broncos player and went on to build a career as a beloved NFL analyst for ESPN, becoming a mainstay of the network's Sunday football programs for three decades, including its "Sunday NFL Countdown" show. He was 75.

Jimmy Pitaro, the chairman of ESPN, praised Jackson in a statement released by the network after his death. In it, Pitaro called Jackson "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history," who "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans."

"Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends," Pitaro said. "Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure."

Jackson's family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wish that his death not be announced until the start of the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show by Jackson's longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman.

"Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom's was frequent and unmistakable," Berman said at the start of the show. "Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too."
Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday.

A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was the inspirational leader of Denver's first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team's second Super Bowl appearance. He was a two-time Associated Press All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler.
Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime."

Before the internet and NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, "NFL Primetime" was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interplay between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other's sentences.

"I can remember coming from games and waiting in a rush to get home, to watch 'Primetime' because all I wanted to know was, what were you and Tom Jackson gonna say about one, the team?" ESPN analyst and Hall of Fame wide receiver Randy Moss said to Berman.

Jackson briefly returned to ESPN in 2019 and reunited with Berman to do an online version of "NFL Primetime." He was awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015.

"In my lifetime there was Howard Cosell doing 'Monday Night Football' halftime highlights and then there were Boomer and TJ doing 'Sunday NFL Countdown.' I am not here as a colleague but as one of million who watched, learned from and idolized the two of you," ESPN host Mike Greenberg said during Sunday's show.
ESPN's studio crew wore orange ties in honor of Jackson during the three-hour show.
Berman said Jackson was the last of seven people interviewed for the studio analyst job and that the last person rarely gets the job. But Jackson nailed the interview.
ESPN's NFL studio in Bristol, Connecticut, is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio. It is the only named studio on ESPN's campus.

"The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history," the Broncos said in a statement.

"An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos' first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country."
Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan.

body_zh: 前橄榄球明星、著名播音员汤姆·杰克逊的家人和 ESPN 周日宣布去世。
杰克逊作为丹佛野马队球员而声名鹊起，随后成为 ESPN 深受喜爱的 NFL 分析师，成为该网络三十年来周日橄榄球节目的中流砥柱，包括其“周日 NFL 倒计时”节目。他75岁了。
ESPN主席吉米·皮塔罗在杰克逊去世后发表的一份声明中赞扬了他。皮塔罗在其中称杰克逊是“ESPN 历史上最有影响力和最受欢迎的人物之一”，他“带来了全职业 NFL 球员的可信度、天才分析师的洞察力以及与几代球迷联系在一起的温暖和真实。”
“他与克里斯·伯曼一起帮助 NFL 黄金时段成为我们橄榄球周末的标志性部分，”皮塔罗说。 “在片场之外，汤姆是许多人值得信赖的同事、慷慨的导师和亲爱的朋友。我们向他的家人、朋友、前队友和所有爱他的人致以最深切的哀悼。他在 ESPN、整个 NFL 以及无数钦佩他令人难以置信的工作的球迷中留下的遗产将持续下去。”
杰克逊的家人告诉 ESPN，他于周五去世，但他们希望在杰克逊的老朋友兼直播搭档克里斯·伯曼 (Chris Berman) 在该网络的“周日 NFL 倒计时”节目开始之前才宣布他的去世消息。
“汤姆不仅仅是一位出色的 NFL 分析师。没有人比他更友善、更体贴、更忠诚或更有吸引力。当谈到笑声时，汤姆的笑声很频繁，而且毫无疑问，”伯曼在节目开始时说道。 “汤姆在职业和个人方面都是我最好的朋友。如果你见过他或者只是通过观看 ESPN 认识他，他也是你最好的朋友。”
伯曼说，杰克逊几周前突然造访了 ESPN，他在为野马队效力了 14 个赛季后，在那里工作了 32 年，两人在周二进行了交谈。
杰克逊是 1973 年路易斯维尔的第四轮选秀球员，是 1977 年丹佛首支超级碗球队的鼓舞人心的领袖。他在 1973-86 年间为野马队首发了 177 场比赛，在球队第二次参加超级碗比赛后退役。他曾两次入选美联社最佳阵容，并三度入选职业投球手。
退役后，Jackson 于 1987 年至 2016 年在 ESPN 开启了第二段职业生涯，并参与了《周日NFL倒计时》（Sunday NFL Countdown）和《NFL黄金时段》（NFL Primetime）的节目。
在互联网和 NBC 于 2006 年接管周日晚间节目之前，《NFL 黄金时段》是球迷和球员必看的节目，因为它展示了所有比赛的精彩片段，以及伯曼和杰克逊之间的互动，他们经常互相补完对方的句子。
“我记得比赛结束后，急急忙忙地等着回家，看‘黄金时段​​’，因为我想知道的是，你和汤姆·杰克逊会对球队说什么？” ESPN 分析师兼名人堂外接手兰迪·莫斯对伯曼说道。
Jackson briefly returned to ESPN in 2019 and reunited with Berman to do an online version of "NFL Primetime." 2015年，他被职业橄榄球名人堂授予皮特·罗泽尔广播电视奖。
“在我的一生中，霍华德·科塞尔 (Howard Cosell) 表演了《周一橄榄球之夜》的中场精彩片段，然后布玛 (Boomer) 和 TJ 表演了《周日 NFL 倒计时》(Sunday NFL Countdown)。我不是作为同事来到这里，而是作为观看你们两人、向你们学习并崇拜你们两人的数百万人中的一员，”ESPN 主持人迈克·格林伯格在周日的节目中说道。
在三个小时的节目中，ESPN 的演播室工作人员都系着橙色领带，以纪念杰克逊。
伯曼说，杰克逊是接受工作室分析师职位面试的七个人中的最后一个，而最后一个人很少能得到这份工作。但杰克逊成功接受了采访。
ESPN 位于康涅狄格州布里斯托尔的 NFL 工作室被命名为克里斯·伯曼-汤姆·杰克逊工作室。它是 ESPN 校园内唯一指定的工作室。
野马队在一份声明中表示：“丹佛野马队对名人堂线卫汤姆·杰克逊的去世感到心碎，他是传奇的 Orange Crush 防守的基石，也是球队历史上最受欢迎的球员之一。”
“TJ 是一位鼓舞人心的领导者和激烈的竞争者，他是野马队第一支超级碗球队的骄傲成员，帮助丹佛建立了获胜传统。在场外，汤姆表现得优雅、热情和谦逊，与队友和整个野马队建立了深厚的联系和终生的友谊。”
杰克逊身后留下了他的妻子詹妮弗以及女儿泰勒和摩根。

body_en: Christian nationalist conference hosts Nick Fuentes, vows to keep pushing MAGA agenda A particular group of Christian nationalists met in Texas last weekend and vowed to push what remains of MAGA as far to the right as possible. They hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes.
A particular group of Christian nationalists met in Texas last weekend and vowed to push what remains of MAGA as far to the right as possible. They hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes.

The midterm election results have some people writing obituaries for the MAGA movement. But last weekend, a particular faction of Christian nationalists got together in Dallas with a plan to push what's left of Trump's coalition as far to the right as possible. NPR's Lisa Hagen was there. And a note - her story contains antisemitic, racist and misogynistic language.
JOEL WEBBON: I'm not demoralized. I'm not defeated, and neither should you be. There will be an America after Trump.

LISA HAGEN, BYLINE: That's Joel Webbon, a pastor from Texas and the man who's organized this event called Christ is King: America after Trump. Webbon's reach on the Christian right has been growing. And this moment, this gathering in Dallas, is another big step for him. Several national news outlets are here. The event has drawn about a thousand attendees. The vast majority are white men. A lot of them are in their 30s and 40s, some with meticulously coiffed beards and mustaches.

WEBBON: Most of you are right-wing. God bless you. Right? You're going to disagree with me because it's like - Joel Webbon's kind of embarrassing. I mean, he's to the left of George Washington. What's the guy even doing?

HAGEN: That's a little joke Webbon likes to use because Washington owned slaves. Webbon claims he believes that there are at least some Black men in America who should retain the right to vote. The conference was filled with similar statements from Webbon and other speakers, which is exactly what the attendees have come to hear for three straight days.
WEBBON: It's not just OK to be white. It's good to be white. Praise God.
HAGEN: Another of Webbon's favorite talking points is repealing women's right to vote, as well as eliminating their place in public life.
WEBBON: Every time you see a woman in leadership, I guarantee there were at least a thousand men who were more qualified for that position than her.
HAGEN: And to top it all off, overt antisemitism.
WEBBON: I'm not trying to be a jerk about this or overly edgy, but the leading cause of the rise of antisemitism remains kind of Jewish behavior.

HAGEN: Webbon is not the pastor of a megachurch. His actual congregation near Austin has about 200 people. But his profile online has spiked as his messages about race, women and Jews have gotten more explicit. He got a big boost earlier this year as he began hosting Nick Fuentes, a 28-year-old far-right streamer and self-described racist and antisemite who's advocated for raping women.

The general branch of Christianity that Webbon is a part of, who call themselves Reformed, is a pretty small group. It's an estimated 2% of Christians in America. But Kristin Kobes Du Mez, a history professor at Calvin University, says she worries that Webbon's influence has begun to break containment from that small Reformed community.

KRISTIN KOBES DU MEZ: Reformed is a Protestant denomination going back to both Martin Luther and especially John Calvin. And the idea that to be a faithful Christian is to shape the rest of society around God's norms - when you accomplish that, then you're going to flourish.

HAGEN: Du Mez herself is Reformed, and she says some in the denomination interpret their religious purpose as the pursuit of social justice. But she says the Joel Webbon branch tends to take what she calls a more coercive approach.

DU MEZ: As a mandate to seize control over all sectors of life and to really freeze out anybody of a different religious faith or of a Christian faith that doesn't align with their understanding, to freeze them out of all positions of power and influence - this is what they mean when they say Christ is king.

一群基督教民族主义者上周末在得克萨斯州举行会议，并发誓要将“MAGA”的残余力量尽可能地推向右翼。他们主持了反犹太主义主播尼克·富恩特斯 (Nick Fuentes)。
中期选举结果让一些人为 MAGA 运动撰写讣告。但上周末，基督教民族主义者的一个特定派系在达拉斯聚集在一起，计划将特朗普联盟的剩余成员尽可能推向右翼。 NPR 的丽莎·哈根也在场。还有一点——她的故事包含反犹太主义、种族主义和厌恶女性的语言。
JOEL WEBBON：我并没有士气低落。我没有被打败，你也不应该被打败。特朗普之后将会有一个美国。
丽莎·哈根连线：这是乔尔·韦本，一位来自得克萨斯州的牧师，他组织了这次名为“基督为王：特朗普之后的美国”的活动。韦本对基督教右翼的影响力不断扩大。而这一刻，这次在达拉斯的聚会，对他来说又是一大步。一些国家新闻媒体都在这里。此次活动吸引了约千名与会者。绝大多数是白人。他们中的许多人年龄在 30 多岁和 40 多岁，有些人留着精心梳理的胡须。
WEBBON：你们大多数人都是右翼分子。上帝保佑你。正确的？你会不同意我的观点，因为乔尔·韦本（Joel Webbon）有点令人尴尬。我的意思是，他在乔治·华盛顿的左边。那家伙到底在做什么？
哈根：这是韦本喜欢开的一个小玩笑，因为华盛顿拥有奴隶。韦邦声称，他相信美国至少有一些黑人应该保留投票权。会议上充斥着 Webbon 和其他演讲者的类似言论，这正是与会者连续三天听到的内容。
WEBBON：不仅仅是白人就可以了。能变白就好了。赞美神。
哈根：韦邦最喜欢的另一个话题是废除妇女的投票权，并消除她们在公共生活中的地位。
WEBBON：每当你看到一位女性担任领导职务时，我保证至少有一千名男性比她更有资格担任该职位。
哈根：最重要的是，公开的反犹太主义。
韦本：我并不是想在这件事上表现得像个混蛋或过于急躁，但反犹太主义兴起的主要原因仍然是犹太人的行为。
哈根：韦本不是大型教会的牧师。他在奥斯汀附近的实际会众约有 200 人。但随着他关于种族、女性和犹太人的信息变得更加明确，他的网上个人资料激增。今年早些时候，他开始主持尼克·富恩特斯(Nick Fuentes)，他获得了巨大的提升。尼克·富恩特斯是一位 28 岁的极右翼主播，自称是种族主义者和反犹太主义者，主张强奸女性。
韦本所属的基督教总分支自称为改革宗，是一个相当小的团体。据估计，美国基督徒中有 2% 是这样的人。但卡尔文大学历史学教授克里斯汀·科比·杜·梅兹表示，她担心韦本的影响力已经开始打破这个小型改革宗社区的遏制。
KRISTIN KOBES DU MEZ：改革宗是一个新教教派，可以追溯到马丁·路德，尤其是约翰·加尔文。成为一名忠实的基督徒就是要围绕上帝的规范塑造社会的其他部分——当你做到这一点时，你就会蓬勃发展。
哈根：杜梅斯本人是改革宗人士，她说该教派中的一些人将他们的宗教目的解释为追求社会正义。但她表示，乔尔·韦本分支机构倾向于采取她所说的更具强制性的方法。
杜梅斯：作为一项命令，要控制生活的各个方面，并真正排除任何不同宗教信仰或不符合他们理解的基督教信仰的人，将他们排除在所有权力和影响力的位置之外——这就是他们说基督为王时的意思。

What to know about Medicare open enrollment this year Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

A counselor, right, helps a client through the Medicare signup process at a resource center for older adults in Sunrise, Florida. Medicare open enrollment season started Oct. 15 and ends Dec. 7. Joe Cavaretta/South Florida Sun Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images
Annual open enrollment is underway for Medicare, the federal program that provides health insurance to roughly 70 million people . The coverage choices are complex and often consequential.
Open enrollment runs through Dec. 7. The plan you choose takes effect on Jan. 1, for the full calendar year.
Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know

Medicare provides health insurance to people 65 or older, as well as to some younger people with disabilities or certain health conditions. But it isn't one plan. It's more like a build-your-own-insurance menu.

Roughly half of beneficiaries are enrolled in traditional Medicare, which consists of Parts A and B. Administered by the federal government, the plan covers hospital stays, skilled nursing care, doctor visits, outpatient care, and preventive screenings. Enrollees can typically see any healthcare provider who accepts Medicare, and they rarely need approval for diagnostic tests, such as MRIs and CT scans. However, there's no cap on out-of-pocket expenses in traditional Medicare, and it doesn't cover most prescriptions or dental, vision, or hearing services.

As a result, most traditional Medicare enrollees buy extra coverage from private insurance companies under Medicare Part D , the prescription drug plan. Some also buy a Medigap policy that covers the costs traditional Medicare leaves behind, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance.

This year, the other half of Medicare beneficiaries opted for privately offered, all-in-one managed-care plans known as Medicare Advantage, usually including prescription drug coverage, dental, and vision. The drawbacks are smaller networks and a greater likelihood that treatments and medications will require prior authorization. Like beneficiaries in traditional Medicare, Medicare Advantage participants also pay Part B premiums.
"People really need to do their research before they enroll in Medicare, because there are trade-offs," said David Lipschutz , a co-director at the Center for Medicare Advocacy.

Every fall, insurers that offer Part D and Advantage plans send enrollees a critical document known as an Annual Notice of Change. It's a cheat sheet outlining what will be different in the following year: premiums, deductibles, covered drugs. Consumer advocates and Medicare experts say people sometimes make the costly mistake of throwing it out or filing it away without reading it. Can't find it? Call the insurer and ask for another copy.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services projects that the average Part D premium will increase less than $1 a month for a standalone prescription drug plan, describing the market as stable. But that average doesn't tell the whole story. An analysis by KFF, the health policy research nonprofit that includes KFF Health News, found that enrollees who stay in their prescription drug plan will see a 50% increase on average, from $34 to $51. About 10.4 million people could pay higher premiums, not including higher deductibles and coinsurance costs.
About 4 million people are in Medicare Advantage plans that won't be offered in 2027. If they do nothing, they'll be automatically enrolled in traditional Medicare. Jenny Kane/AP hide caption

Some beneficiaries who didn't have to pay monthly premiums in recent years will begin paying for prescription drug Part D coverage in 2027. While that change follows the 2025 introduction of federal caps on out-of-pocket drug expenses, it comes as the Trump administration is ending temporary federal subsidies that helped keep premiums down. The cap on out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs in 2027 will be $2,400, a total enrollees can opt to spread out over the course of the year.
Juliette Cubanski, who directs the Program on Medicare Policy at KFF, said people who don't shop around could be leaving money on the table.
"It is worth it to avoid any unpleasant surprises in the form of either higher premiums or higher cost sharing for covered services in 2027," she said.

An estimated 4.3 million people now have to look for a new Medicare Advantage or prescription drug plan after private insurers left the market. Those who want to stay in Medicare Advantage must select new coverage, or they'll be moved to traditional Medicare automatically. For those shopping for a new plan, low monthly premiums may be appealing, but it's important to read the fine print and add up the other costs.

"There are going to be, often, increases in cost sharing and copays, increases in out-of-pocket caps, and reductions in the scope of some of the extra benefits that Medicare Advantage plans provide," Lipschutz said.
body_zh: 关于今年医疗保险开放注册的信息：NPR
关于今年 Medicare 开放注册的信息 Medicare 开放注册截止日期为 12 月 7 日，人们今年应该注意一些不同的陷阱。您的药物计划或 Medicare Advantage 计划可能会发生很大变化。
一名顾问（右）在佛罗里达州日出市的老年人资源中心帮助客户完成医疗保险注册流程。医疗保险开放投保季于 10 月 15 日开始，12 月 7 日结束。Joe Cavaretta/南佛罗里达太阳哨兵/论坛新闻服务来自 Getty Images
医疗保险年度公开报名正在进行中，这是一项为大约 7000 万人提供健康保险的联邦计划。承保范围的选择很复杂，而且往往很重要。
开放注册截止日期为 12 月 7 日。您选择的计划将于 1 月 1 日生效，适用于整个日历年。
您的 Medicare Advantage 计划明年结束吗？这是你需要知道的
Medicare 为 65 岁或以上的人以及一些患有残疾或某些健康问题的年轻人提供健康保险。但这不是一个计划。它更像是一个构建您自己的保险菜单。
大约一半的受益人参加了传统医疗保险，该医疗保险由 A 部分和 B 部分组成。该计划由联邦政府管理，涵盖住院、专业护理、医生就诊、门诊护理和预防性检查。参保者通常可以去看任何接受 Medicare 的医疗保健提供者，他们很少需要批准诊断测试，例如 MRI 和 CT 扫描。然而，传统医疗保险中的自付费用没有上限，并且不承保大多数处方或牙科、视力或听力服务。
因此，大多数传统 Medicare 参保者根据 Medicare D 部分（处方药计划）从私人保险公司购买额外保险。有些人还购买 Medigap 保单，涵盖传统 Medicare 留下的费用，例如免赔额、共付额和共同保险。
今年，另一半医疗保险受益人选择了私人提供的一体化管理医疗计划，称为医疗保险优势，通常包括处方药保险、牙科和视力保险。缺点是网络较小，并且治疗和药物更有可能需要事先授权。与传统 Medicare 的受益人一样，Medicare Advantage 参与者也支付 B 部分保费。
医疗保险倡导中心联合主任大卫·利普舒茨 (David Lipschutz) 表示：“人们在加入医疗保险之前确实需要进行研究，因为这其中存在权衡。”
每年秋天，提供 D 部分和 Advantage 计划的保险公司都会向参保者发送一份重要文件，称为年度变更通知。这是一份备忘单，概述了来年的不同之处：保费、免赔额、承保药物。消费者权益倡导者和医疗保险专家表示，人们有时会犯一个代价高昂的错误，即在没有阅读的情况下将其扔掉或归档。找不到吗？致电保险公司并索要另一份副本。
医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心预计，独立处方药计划的 D 部分保费平均每月增加不到 1 美元，表明市场稳定。但这个平均值并不能说明全部情况。 KFF（包括 KFF Health News 在内的健康政策研究非营利组织）的一项分析发现，继续参与处方药计划的参与者的平均费用将增加 50%，从 34 美元增至 51 美元。大约 1040 万人可以支付更高的保费，这还不包括更高的免赔额和共同保险费用。
大约有 400 万人加入了 Medicare Advantage 计划，但到 2027 年将不再提供。如果他们不采取任何行动，他们将自动加入传统 Medicare。珍妮·凯恩/美联社隐藏标题栏
近年来不需要每月支付保费的一些受益人将从 2027 年开始支付处方药 D 部分承保费用。虽然这一变化是在 2025 年对自付费用药品费用实行联邦上限之后进行的，但与此同时，特朗普政府正在终止有助于压低保费的临时联邦补贴。 2027 年处方药自付费用上限为 2,400 美元，参保人数可以选择在一年内分摊。
KFF 医疗保险政策项目负责人朱丽叶特·库班斯基 (Juliette Cubanski) 表示，不货比三家的人可能会白白浪费钱。
她说：“为了避免 2027 年承保服务保费上涨或分摊费用上涨等令人不快的意外情况，这是值得的。”
在私人保险公司退出市场后，估计有 430 万人现在不得不寻找新的 Medicare Advantage 或处方药计划。那些想要继续享受 Medicare Advantage 的人必须选择新的承保范围，否则他们将自动转至传统的 Medicare。对于那些购买新计划的人来说，每月的低保费可能很有吸引力，但阅读细则并计算其他费用也很重要。
利普舒茨说：“通常情况下，费用分摊和共付额会增加，自付费用上限会增加，医疗保险优势计划提供的一些额外福利的范围也会减少。”

title_en: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
title_zh: 化石燃料争论引发争议后，联合国气候峰会未达成协议
summary: COP31, the latest installment of the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed.
summary_zh: 最新一届联合国年度气候会议 COP31 在经过数天有争议的谈判后于周日结束，但未达成最终协议
body_en: COP31, the United Nations' annual climate conference , ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed, mainly because of disputes between nations pushing to phase out fossil fuel use and others opposed to doing so.

The breakdown capped two weeks of negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, between delegations from nearly 200 countries. Their debates ran into overtime, becoming the longest COP summit in history, at a moment that U.N. officials and many scientists have called decisive for the trajectory of global warming and climate change.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement that Sunday he was "deeply disappointed" by the outcome of the summit.

"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," he said. "But this setback does not change the facts. There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."

The United States sent no representatives to the climate conference for the second year in a row , following the Trump administration's withdrawal from the 2015 Paris Agreement. That accord set a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, a target that has anchored every U.N. climate summit since and that the world is now poised to overshoot .
Talks reached an impasse Sunday, as the European Union opposed a draft agreement that failed to mention fossil fuels and which, its delegates argued, placated countries that export them.

"We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuel, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU in Antalya. "And we will not accept negotiating backward in time, and we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel."

The EU joined a group of smaller nations facing heightened threats of climate extremes and challenged oil producers, like Saudi Arabia, that staunchly rejected their views. The finale came after days of tense discussions over some of the core topics at issue during the summit, including whether to establish new rules and goals around transitioning away from coal, oil and natural gas in favor of renewable energy.

COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey's environmental minister, said in televised comments from Antalya on Sunday that a draft had not been adopted due to a lack of consensus. The conference rules require unanimous agreement to reach a deal, so even a single nation's dissent can derail the process.

"We have always emphasized that this process is one that respects the will of the parties. We did everything we could," Kurum said. "In the end, we did not impose this text on anyone. We did not pressure anyone with a take-it-or-leave-it approach. There are parties in the hall that oppose this text, and we see that there is no agreement on it. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted."

Australia's climate and energy minister Chris Bowen, who shared the COP31 presidency with Kurum as Turkey and Australia jointly hosted this year's summit, said Sunday that talks broke down because of "unbridgeable red lines" and added that "the situation coming into this COP was the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory," reported CBS partner BBC News.

On Friday, the scheduled final day of the conference, a coalition led by France and Panama and including countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific rejected the latest draft agreement as too weak, according to the U.N . The group demanded explicit language on fossil fuels and stronger commitments on climate finance.

"We cannot continue to be held hostage by petroleum producers," said Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, at a news conference last week. He also vowed that Panama would formally object to any deal omitting issues related to fossil fuels.

An initial draft of negotiators' agreement had called for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels," a recurring goal at these summits, and urged an end to inefficient fossil fuel subsidies. It also resolved to bring warming back below 1.5 degrees as early as possible this century. But that language was gone days later, reflecting deep divisions over timelines and financing.

Later drafts still did not contain language about fossil fuels, although they did include proposed targets to capture billions of tons of carbon dioxide annually from the atmosphere by 2035, using technology that critics have said distracts from the need to cut fossil fuel use. They also called for electricity to supply more than a third of the world's energy by the same deadline, alongside goals around renewable energy and energy efficiency.

Negotiators had expressed "deep concern" in drafted text over global warming, which at its peak is projected to exceed 1.5 degrees. They also reaffirmed the need "for deep, rapid and sustained emissions reductions," warning that every increment of additional warming will increase the frequency and intensity of climate-related loss and damage. If current international climate plans were fully implemented, they noted, the world would be on track for just over 2.5 degrees of warming, down from projections of more than 4 degrees before the Paris accord.

The COP31 summit unfolded in a year marked by deadly disasters , record heat , destructive wildfires, tumultuous surf and other anomalies, which meteorologists have largely tied to a powerful El Niño . Scientists say its effects are amplified by climate change.

Speaking in Antalya last week, Guterres urged governments to move away from fossil fuels, triple adaptation funding by 2035 and tax fossil fuel companies' windfall profits to help vulnerable nations recover from disasters. "Polluters must pay," he said. At a press conference two days later, he linked the climate crisis to deeper social and political instability.

"You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it," Guterres said. "You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends. And you cannot speak seriously about justice when those who did least to cause the crisis suffer first and worst."
Some environmental advocates felt the conference proposals didn't go far enough to meet the needs of communities that are already facing real consequences of the climate crisis.
body_zh: 联合国年度气候会议第 31 次缔约方会议 (COP31) 于周日结束，但在数日有争议的谈判破裂后，会议未能达成最终协议，这主要是因为推动逐步淘汰化石燃料使用的国家与反对这样做的其他国家之间存在争议。
这次谈判的破裂导致来自近 200 个国家的代表团在土耳其安塔利亚举行的为期两周的谈判结束。他们的辩论陷入加时，成为历史上最长的缔约方会议峰会，联合国官员和许多科学家称此时此刻对全球变暖和气候变化的轨迹具有决定性作用。
联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯周日在一份声明中表示，他对峰会的结果“深感失望”。
他说：“我和所有那些期望政府在应对气候危机时采取行动的人一样感到非常沮丧。” “但这次挫折并不能改变事实。谈判室里可能没有达成共识。科学上没有任何含糊之处。”
自特朗普政府退出2015年《巴黎协定》后，美国连续第二年没有派出代表出席气候大会。该协议设定了将气温升高限制在比工业化前水平高出 1.5 摄氏度的目标，此后历届联合国气候峰会都以此为基础，而世界现在正准备超越这一目标。
周日谈判陷入僵局，欧盟反对一项未提及化石燃料的协议草案，欧盟代表认为该草案安抚了化石燃料出口国。
爱尔兰气候部长达拉·奥布莱恩在安塔利亚代表欧盟发言时表示：“我们不会支持甚至不提及化石燃料的封面决定或安塔利亚协议，化石燃料是气候变化的关键驱动因素。” “我们不会接受时间倒退的谈判，我们也不会接受对化石燃料进行绿色清洗的缔约方会议。”
欧盟加入了一些面临极端气候严重威胁的小国行列，并对沙特阿拉伯等石油生产国提出了挑战，这些国家坚决拒绝他们的观点。峰会结束前，就峰会期间的一些核心议题进行了数天的紧张讨论，其中包括是否制定从煤炭、石油和天然气转向可再生能源的新规则和目标。
COP31主席、土耳其环境部长穆拉特·库鲁姆周日在安塔利亚的电视评论中表示，由于缺乏共识，草案尚未获得通过。会议规则要求一致同意才能达成协议，因此即使一个国家的异议也可能会破坏这一进程。
“我们一直强调，这一进程是尊重各方意愿的进程。我们已竭尽全力，”库鲁姆说。 “最后，我们没有把这个案文强加给任何人。我们没有以要么接受要么放弃的方式向任何人施加压力。大厅里有反对这个案文的政党，我们看到没有就它达成一致。因此，这些决定没有被通过。”
据哥伦比亚广播公司合作伙伴英国广播公司新闻报道，澳大利亚气候和能源部长克里斯·鲍文周日表示，由于“不可逾越的红线”，谈判破裂，并补充说，“本届缔约方会议的局势是人们记忆中最复杂、最令人担忧的地缘政治环境。”
据联合国称，周五，即会议预定的最后一天，由法国和巴拿马领导、包括欧洲、非洲、拉丁美洲和太平洋国家在内的联盟拒绝了最新的协议草案，因为该草案过于软弱。该组织要求就化石燃料发表明确的措辞，并对气候融资作出更强有力的承诺。
“我们不能继续被石油生产商扣为人质，”巴拿马环境部长胡安·卡洛斯·纳瓦罗在上周的新闻发布会上表示。他还誓言巴拿马将正式反对任何忽略化石燃料相关问题的协议。
谈判代表协议的初步草案呼吁“加速行动，逐步淘汰化石燃料”，这是这些峰会上反复出现的目标，并敦促结束低效的化石燃料补贴。它还决心在本世纪尽早将气温升高控制在 1.5 度以下。但几天后这种语言就消失了，反映出时间表和融资方面的深刻分歧。
后来的草案仍然没有包含有关化石燃料的措辞，尽管它们确实包含了到 2035 年每年从大气中捕获数十亿吨二氧化碳的拟议目标，批评者称使用的技术分散了人们对减少化石燃料使用的注意力。他们还呼吁在同一期限内电力供应世界三分之一以上的能源，同时实现可再生能源和能源效率的目标。
谈判代表在草案文本中对全球变暖表示“深切关注”，全球变暖预计在峰值时将超过 1.5 度。他们还重申需要“深度、快速和持续的减排”，并警告说，每一次进一步的变暖都会增加与气候相关的损失和损害的频率和强度。他们指出，如果当前的国际气候计划得到全面实施，全球气温将上升 2.5 度多一点，低于《巴黎协定》之前预测的 4 度多。
COP31峰会召开的这一年，发生了致命的灾难、创纪录的高温、破坏性的野火、汹涌的海浪和其他异常现象，气象学家将这些现象很大程度上与强大的厄尔尼诺现象联系在一起。科学家表示，气候变化会放大其影响。
古特雷斯上周在安塔利亚发表讲话，敦促各国政府放弃化石燃料，到2035年将适应资金增加三倍，并对化石燃料公司的暴利征税，以帮助脆弱国家从灾难中恢复。 “污染者必须付出代价，”他说。在两天后的新闻发布会上，他将气候危机与更深层次的社会和政治不稳定联系起来。
古特雷斯说：“当气候灾难不断让人们陷入贫困时，你就无法消除贫困。” “你不能向年轻人承诺一个更美好的未来，同时却破坏了未来所依赖的自然系统。当那些对造成危机影响最小的人首先遭受最严重的痛苦时，你就不能严肃地谈论正义。”
一些环保倡导者认为，会议提案还不足以满足已经面临气候危机实际后果的社区的需求。

title_en: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
title_zh: 不要喂动物。兽医解释了为什么帽子、硬币和鞋子可能致命。
summary: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.
summary_zh: 一旦动物误食异物，就很难将其取出。有些东西可以使用内窥镜抓取。但如果某件物品深入
body_en: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly. It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.

Fiona, a Nile Hippopotamus, eats her specialty birthday cake to celebrate turning three-years old this Friday, in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, Thursday, Jan. 23, 2020, in Cincinnati. John Minchillo/AP hide caption
The death of Fiona, a beloved hippopotamus who captured hearts, has renewed calls to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.

Fiona, 9 years old, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat at the Cincinnati Zoo. The zoo said that the hat was lodged in the hippo's small intestine and surgery was not possible.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement .
While deaths are rare, items such as coins, shoes and sunglasses frequently fall, and sometimes are tossed, into animal enclosures.

In 2024, 70 U.S. coins were successfully removed from an alligator at Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium. And in 2025, a Komodo dragon ate a shoe that was thrown into its habitat at the Memphis Zoo. The shoe was removed and the dragon survived.
Dr. Gabriella Flacke, an associate veterinarian at Zoo Miami, said the zoo's staff have retrieved items such as cellphones from alligators.

"We've had to remove those items both endoscopically, which is basically putting a camera through the mouth and down into the stomach to grab and retrieve those items, or we've in a few cases had to do surgery where they were larger items that couldn't be removed that way," Flacke told NPR.
Fiona, a baby Nile Hippopotamus swims in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, in Cincinnati, June 26, 2018. John Minchillo/AP hide caption

Recovering items from an alligator is easier than a hippo, she said. Unlike the alligator, which has a digestive system with one stomach divided into two parts, hippos have a multichambered stomach. This can make retrieving objects, such as the small hat that Fiona ingested, difficult, according to Dr. Jen Quammen, president of the American Veterinary Medical Association.
"It's not necessarily always the shape or size of the object, but it's maybe the twists and turns, metaphorically and physiologically, that things have to go through," Quammen told NPR.

Be aware that the animals have specialized dietary needs and requirements that caretakers provide them, Flacke said. She also asked visitors to follow zoo etiquette and not yell or throw objects at the animals.

"Anything that we bring that could inadvertently end up in the animal exhibit or somehow around the animal, try to just be mindful and not have your sunglasses on your head if you're leaning over and looking at something," she said. "If your child has a toy in its hand and you're walking around, it could just decide to throw the toy, whether it's thinking about that or not."
Both Quammen and Flacke said people should not only be mindful of items that can harm animals at the zoo, but also what could hurt animals in the wild or pets at home.
Animals explore the world by putting things in their mouths, making them naturally curious about items that can be dangerous, Quammen said.
Giraffe Ellish is fed with a vegetarian kebab at London Zoo, Thursday, June 1, 2017. = Frank Augstein/AP hide caption
To help prevent an animal from ingesting something dangerous, one should dispose of their trash and properly store items such as human medicines in a place where an animal cannot reach it.
body_zh: 不要喂动物。兽医解释了为什么帽子、硬币和鞋子可能致命。一旦动物误食异物，就很难将其取出。有些东西可以使用内窥镜抓取。但如果异物深入肠道，手术并不总是可行。
2020 年 1 月 23 日星期四，尼罗河河马菲奥娜本周五在辛辛那提动植物园的围栏里吃着她特制的生日蛋糕来庆祝三岁生日。约翰·明奇洛/美联社隐藏标题栏
菲奥娜 (Fiona) 是一只深受人们喜爱的河马，它的死亡再次引发人们的注意，提醒动物园游客动物可能会因吞咽异物而死亡。
周四，9 岁的菲奥娜 (Fiona) 在辛辛那提动物园的栖息地误食了一顶帽子后死亡。动物园表示，帽子卡在河马的小肠里，无法进行手术。
辛辛那提动物园园长戴夫·詹尼克在一份声明中说：“我们的动物护理团队英勇地努力拯救她。他们竭尽全力，但她的身体再也无法抵抗了。”
虽然死亡事件很少见，但硬币、鞋子和太阳镜等物品经常掉落，有时甚至被扔进动物围栏中。
2024 年，奥马哈亨利多立动物园和水族馆的鳄鱼身上成功取出了 70 枚美国硬币。 2025 年，一只科莫多巨蜥吃了一只被扔进孟菲斯动物园栖息地的鞋子。鞋子被脱掉，龙幸免于难。
迈阿密动物园的副兽医加布里埃拉·弗拉克博士表示，动物园的工作人员已经从鳄鱼身上取回了手机等物品。
弗莱克告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“我们必须通过内窥镜取出这些物品，这基本上就是将摄像头从嘴里放入胃中，以抓住并取回这些物品，或者在少数情况下，我们不得不进行手术，因为它们是无法通过这种方式取出的较大物品。”
2018 年 6 月 26 日，辛辛那提动物园和植物园的小尼罗河马菲奥娜在她的围栏里游泳。约翰·明奇洛/美联社 隐藏标题栏
她说，从鳄鱼身上找回物品比从河马身上找回更容易。与鳄鱼的消化系统不同，河马的胃分为两个部分，而河马的胃是多室的。美国兽医协会主席珍·夸曼 (Jen Quammen) 博士表示，这可能会导致检索物体变得困难，例如菲奥娜吞下的小帽子。
夸曼告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“事情必须经历的不一定总是物体的形状或大小，但从隐喻和生理角度来说，这可能是事物必须经历的曲折。”
弗莱克说，请注意，这些动物有特殊的饮食需求和饲养员为它们提供的要求。她还要求游客遵守动物园礼仪，不要对动物大喊大叫或扔东西。
“我们带来的任何东西都可能不经意地出现在动物展览中或以某种方式出现在动物周围，请尽量保持警惕，如果你弯腰看东西，不要把太阳镜戴在头上，”她说。 “如果你的孩子手里拿着一个玩具，而你正在四处走动，它可能会决定扔掉玩具，无论它是否考虑到这一点。”
夸门和弗莱克都表示，人们不仅应该注意可能伤害动物园动物的物品，还应该注意可能伤害野生动物或家中宠物的物品。
夸门说，动物通过把东西放进嘴里来探索世界，这让它们天生对可能危险的东西感到好奇。
2017 年 6 月 1 日，星期四，长颈鹿埃利什在伦敦动物园吃素食烤肉串。= Frank Augstein/美联社 隐藏标题栏
为了防止动物摄入危险的东西，人们应该处理垃圾，并将人类药物等物品妥善存放在动物接触不到的地方。

title_en: ‘Grandfather’ or ‘godfather’? Republicans know they’re stuck with Trump
title_zh: “祖父”还是“干爹”？共和党人知道他们被特朗普困住了
summary: Some grassroots GOP leaders want Trump to stay out of 2028 — even though they know he won’t.
summary_zh: 一些草根共和党领导人希望特朗普远离 2028 年——尽管他们知道他不会。
body_en: Republican leaders grappling with how to recover after their devastating midterm losses agree on one thing: President Donald Trump isn't going anywhere in 2028, even if some wish he would.

Interviews with more than two dozen GOP state and county officials from red, blue and purple states across the country conducted since Election Day revealed a party still processing their election drubbing and at a loss for how to move forward. Some want to move on from Trump entirely. Some are eager for his involvement. And others are just resigned that he’s going to do whatever he wants, regardless of their preferences.

All of them are worried about the party’s chances of retaining control of the White House in two short years, but they also recognize its current occupant is going to continue to exercise a huge role in the future of the party.

“President Trump is going to be part of it, whether we want that or not,” said Arkansas GOP chair Joseph Wood. “His voters are still going to be Republicans that we need to have come out in this election in two years.”

That leaves the party in a precarious position. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found the president’s approval rating at 32% overall, and at 70% among Republicans — down from 91% on inauguration day last year. A POLITICO Poll taken after the midterms found 56% of Trump’s 2024 voters believe the Republican Party needs to distance itself from him and his agenda. But no one in the party expects that to happen. And Trump has already taken steps to maintain his grip on the GOP, endorsing Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters for another term and ordering his powerful super PAC to continue fundraising ahead of 2028.
A handful of Republican grassroots leaders were openly critical of Trump.
“I don't know how much he really has to offer,” said Vermont GOP chair Paul Dame. “I think most people are ready to move on in a new direction.”
Added Michael Bub, the chair of ruby-red Taylor County, Wisconsin, Republican Party :“He should stay out of it. Look at the people he endorsed: They lost.”
In a statement, RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassare said “President Trump remains the unequivocal leader of our party.”

“Republicans will continue to harness his ability to energize our voters and expose the Democrats' disastrous record to win in 2028,” she said. The White House demurred, pointing to the RNC’s response.
Many party officials are resigned to Trump doing whatever he wants, given his domineering personality and strong sway over the party base.
Nebraska Republican Party Chair Mary Jane Truemper said “Donald Trump's going to play whatever role he wants to play.”
“He's the president,” Truemper said. “I look at things as they are and not as I want them to be.”
That’s leaving some state-level Republican leaders wanting the president to take on a more constructive role and be willing to let other candidates and ideas rise.

“I hope he becomes kind of the mentor grandfather, and not the godfather,” said Kansas GOP chair Danedri Herbert. “In America, we hope and expect our presidents to not keep a tight grip on the party, to recognize that now it's time for me to mentor the next generation.”

Added outgoing Minnesota Republican Party Chair Alex Plechash: “We need to capitalize on what he brought to the party and do what we can to retain that. But there has been a definite turn in the political landscape.”
Virtually every GOP official cited the poor political environment caused in part by the president’s handling of the economy and the war in Iran as the reason for the party’s midterm meltdown.
But many stopped short of laying the blame directly at the president’s feet, a sign of how criticism of Trump is still verboten within the party.
“I don't want to play the blame game, because I just don't think it's productive,” said West Virginia GOP chair Josh Holstein. “But I do think that it was more economics than it was anything.”

Many GOP chairs praised the president’s ability to bring in new voters to the party and credited him for working to turn those voters out on behalf of other candidates. Still, some said they hope Trump’s generation-defining tenure at the top of the party comes to an end, allowing Republicans to choose the nominee without his influence.
body_zh: 正在努力解决中期选举惨败后如何恢复的共和党领导人一致同意一件事：唐纳德·特朗普总统在 2028 年不会去任何地方，即使有些人希望他这么做。
自选举日以来对来自全国红州、蓝州和紫州的两打共和党州和县官员进行的采访显示，该党仍在处理选举惨败的情况，并且不知道如何继续前进。有些人希望完全摆脱特朗普。有些人渴望他的参与。而其他人则只能听天由命，认为他会做任何他想做的事，不管他们的喜好如何。
他们所有人都担心该党在短短两年内保住白宫控制权的机会，但他们也认识到现任白宫主人将继续在该党的未来中发挥巨大作用。
阿肯色州共和党主席约瑟夫·伍德表示：“无论我们是否愿意，特朗普总统都将参与其中。” “他的选民仍然是共和党人，我们需要在两年后的这次选举中站出来。”

这使得该党处于岌岌可危的境地。路透社/益普索最近的一项民意调查显示，总统的整体支持率为 32%，共和党人的支持率为 70%，低于去年就职当天的 91%。中期选举后进行的一项政治民意调查显示，2024 年特朗普的选民中有 56% 认为共和党需要与他和他的议程保持距离。但党内没有人预计这种情况会发生。特朗普已经采取措施维持对共和党的控制，支持共和党全国委员会主席乔·格鲁特斯连任，并命令其强大的超级政治行动委员会在 2028 年之前继续筹款。
一些共和党基层领导人公开批评特朗普。
“我不知道他到底能提供多少，”佛蒙特州共和党主席保罗·戴姆 (Paul Dame) 说。 “我认为大多数人已经准备好朝着新的方向前进。”
威斯康星州红宝石泰勒县共和党主席迈克尔·布布补充道：“他应该置身事外。看看他支持的人：他们输了。”
共和党全国委员会发言人娜塔莉·巴尔达萨雷在一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统仍然是我们党明确的领导人。”
“共和党人将继续利用他的能力来激励我们的选民并揭露民主党的灾难性记录，以便在 2028 年获胜，”她说。白宫对此表示反对，并指出了共和党全国委员会的回应。
鉴于特朗普的霸道个性和对党内基础的强大影响力，许多党内官员已经听任特朗普为所欲为。
内布拉斯加州共和党主席玛丽·简·特鲁姆珀表示：“唐纳德·特朗普将扮演他想扮演的任何角色。”
“他是总统，”特鲁姆珀说。 “I look at things as they are and not as I want them to be.”
这使得一些州级共和党领导人希望总统发挥更具建设性的作用，并愿意让其他候选人和想法崛起。
堪萨斯州共和党主席丹德里·赫伯特说：“我希望他成为祖父的导师，而不是教父。” “在美国，我们希望并期望我们的总统不要对党保持严格控制，要认识到现在是我指导下一代的时候了。”
即将离任的明尼苏达州共和党主席亚历克斯·普莱查什补充道：“我们需要利用他给党带来的东西，并尽我们所能来保留这一点。但政治格局已经发生了明显的转变。”
几乎每一位共和党官员都将总统处理经济和伊朗战争造成的恶劣政治环境视为该党中期崩溃的原因。
但许多人并没有直接将责任归咎于总统，这表明党内仍然禁止批评特朗普。
“我不想玩指责游戏，因为我认为这没有成效，”西弗吉尼亚州共和党主席乔什·霍尔斯坦说。 “但我确实认为这更多的是出于经济考虑。”
许多共和党主席赞扬总统为党带来新选民的能力，并赞扬他为其他候选人驱逐这些选民所做的努力。尽管如此，一些人表示，他们希望特朗普在党内高层的决定性任期能够结束，让共和党人能够在不受他影响的情况下选择提名人。

title_en: Trump's top intelligence official is also taking charge of cyber policy
title_zh: 特朗普的最高情报官员也负责网络政策
summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned. A White House official said the strong support Davies received convinced Trum
summary_zh: 国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 也将担任代理国家网络总监，而克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 则等待参议院确认任命。
body_en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned.
A White House official said the strong support Davies received convinced Trump to nominate her to lead the office permanently rather than keep her in an acting capacity.

Why it matters: Clayton, the nation's top intelligence official, will now coordinate cybersecurity policy as outages and reported cyberattacks expose vulnerabilities in America's digital infrastructure.
Catch up quick: President Trump announced Thursday he was tapping Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to replace Sean Cairncross as national cyber director.
Davies will assist Clayton as a senior adviser in the Office of the National Cyber Director until she is confirmed.

Trump has increasingly turned to Clayton. He became director of national intelligence in August, and then Trump named him AI czar coordinating the government's approach to AI. Now he will temporarily lead the office responsible for coordinating cybersecurity policy.

What they're saying: "I'm excited to work more with Kirsten, who has the experience and capabilities needed to help America navigate our increasingly complex and powerful digital infrastructure as our next National Cyber Director," Clayton said in a statement to Axios.
"I look forward to working with the ONCD team to ensure Kirsten has a seamless transition into the role upon her confirmation by the Senate."
The big picture: Two critical national security roles will temporarily fall under one official as President Trump shakes up his cybersecurity team amid the growing threat of AI-powered attacks.

The disruptions have raised concerns about the vulnerability of the nation's digital infrastructure, although administration officials say there is no evidence they were caused by coordinated cyberattacks.
Clayton himself has played a prominent role in the administration's response, telling lawmakers Wednesday that the outages appeared to stem from unrelated technical problems and system upgrades.
Driving the news: Clayton spent Sunday morning on CNN's "State of the Union," ABC's "This Week" and "Fox News Sunday," explaining recent technology disruptions and national security concerns.
On CNN, he warned that Americans should expect more "glitches, gaps, interruptions in service" as government agencies and businesses modernize their systems.
On ABC, Clayton maintained that recent widespread outages were neither coordinated nor state-sponsored, but declined to discuss reported cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture.
On Fox News, he said AI is giving malicious actors more powerful tools and warned that critical infrastructure will need upgrades.
Zoom in: Davies oversees the Pentagon's information technology and cybersecurity strategy, including efforts to modernize aging systems and protect military networks.
She has nearly two decades of technology experience, including senior roles at Unilever, Estée Lauder, Barclays Africa, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Siemens.

Behind the scenes: Clayton has already worked closely with the Office of the National Cyber Director, National Security Council, National Security Agency and other agencies through his AI leadership role, according to the White House official.
body_zh: Axios 获悉，国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 还将担任代理国家网络总监，而克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 正在等待参议院确认领导该办公室。
一名白宫官员表示，戴维斯获得的大力支持使特朗普决定提名她永久领导该办公室，而不是让她担任代理职务。
为什么重要：美国最高情报官员克莱顿现在将协调网络安全政策，因为中断和报道的网络攻击暴露了美国数字基础设施的漏洞。
快速赶上：特朗普总统周四宣布，他将任命五角大楼首席信息官戴维斯接替肖恩·凯恩克罗斯担任国家网络总监。
戴维斯将在国家网络总监办公室担任高级顾问协助克莱顿，直至她得到确认。
特朗普越来越多地转向克莱顿。他于 8 月成为国家情报总监，然后特朗普任命他为人工智能沙皇，协调政府对人工智能的处理方式。现在他将暂时领导负责协调网络安全政策的办公室。
克莱顿在给 Axios 的一份声明中表示：“我很高兴能与克尔斯滕进行更多合作，作为我们的下一任国家网络总监，她拥有帮助美国驾驭日益复杂和强大的数字基础设施所需的经验和能力。”
“我期待与 ONCD 团队合作，确保 Kirsten 在参议院确认后顺利过渡到该职位。”
大局：随着人工智能攻击威胁日益严重，特朗普总统重组了他的网络安全团队，两个关键的国家安全职责将暂时由一名官员负责。
这些中断引发了人们对国家数字基础设施脆弱性的担忧，尽管政府官员表示，没有证据表明这些中断是由协调一致的网络攻击造成的。
克莱顿本人在政府的应对措施中发挥了重要作用，他周三告诉立法者，停电似乎源于不相关的技术问题和系统升级。
推动新闻传播：克莱顿周日上午在 CNN 的《国情咨文》、ABC 的《本周》和《福克斯周日新闻》节目中解释了最近的技术中断和国家安全问题。
他在美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）上警告说，随着政府机构和企业对其系统进行现代化改造，美国人应该预料到会出现更多“故障、差距和服务中断”。
在美国广播公司 (ABC) 上，克莱顿坚称，最近的大范围停电既不是协调的，也不是国家支持的，但拒绝讨论联邦调查局和农业部所报告的网络攻击。
他在福克斯新闻上表示，人工智能正在为恶意行为者提供更强大的工具，并警告说关键基础设施需要升级。
放大：戴维斯负责监督五角大楼的信息技术和网络安全战略，包括对老化系统进行现代化改造和保护军事网络的努力。
她拥有近二十年的技术经验，包括在联合利华、雅诗兰黛、巴克莱非洲、惠普企业和西门子担任高级职务。
幕后：据白宫官员称，克莱顿已经通过其人工智能领导角色与国家网络主任办公室、国家安全委员会、国家安全局和其他机构密切合作。

title_en: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
title_zh: 气候会议谈判破裂时的感觉
summary: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
summary_zh: 经过两周的谈判，国际气候谈判未能达成协议。 NPR 的 Rachel Waldholz 正在土耳其参加这次会议。
body_en: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
What it's like in the halls of a climate conference as it collapses
After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended today after negotiations fell apart. NPR's Rachel Waldholz has been at the conference and sent us this report.

RACHEL WALDHOLZ, BYLINE: I'm here in the Antalya Expo Center, which, for the past two weeks, has been packed with some 70,000 people who came to the COP31 climate conference. Now it's almost completely empty. In fact, they're disassembling parts of the venue around me. The climate talks ran two days past their scheduled end. By the time the gavel fell, many negotiators had already left to catch their flights home. Australia climate chief Chris Bowen led the negotiations.
CHRIS BOWEN: I haven't slept for the last three nights, been negotiating all the way through, but more importantly, people on delegations came at it and gave it everything they had.

WALDHOLZ: Delegates came to Antalya with long wish lists, from electrifying more of the global economy to money for developing countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change. Looming over it all is that this is the first summit to squarely face the reality that the planet will miss a key target of the Paris Climate Agreement, reaching warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above pre-Industrial levels. The U.N. says limiting that overshoot requires cutting the use of fossil fuels nearly in half in the next 10 to 15 years. Many countries wanted an agreement explicitly calling for a transition away from coal, oil and natural gas. But big oil-producing countries, like Saudi Arabia, blocked any mention of fossil fuels. Ultimately, the European Union decided no deal was better than the deal on the table. Darragh O'Brien is Ireland's environment minister.
DARRAGH O'BRIEN: We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.

WALDHOLZ: Many negotiators left the expo center dragging their suitcases on the way to the airport. They'll pick up negotiations next year at the next climate summit in Ethiopia. I'm Rachel Waldholz in Antalya, Turkey.

经过两周的谈判，国际气候谈判未能达成协议。 NPR 的 Rachel Waldholz 正在土耳其参加这次会议。
在土耳其安塔利亚举行的国际气候谈判在谈判破裂后于今天结束。 NPR 的 Rachel Waldholz 出席了会议并向我们发送了这份报告。
雷切尔·瓦尔德霍兹连线：我现在在安塔利亚博览中心，过去两周，这里挤满了大约 70,000 名前来参加 COP31 气候会议的人。现在它几乎完全是空的。事实上，他们正在拆除我周围场地的部分区域。气候谈判比原定结束时间晚了两天。当木槌落下时，许多谈判代表已经出发搭乘航班回家。澳大利亚气候主管克里斯·鲍文领导了此次谈判。
克里斯·鲍文：过去三个晚上我没有睡觉，一直在谈判，但更重要的是，代表团成员都来了，并付出了他们所拥有的一切。

WALDHOLZ：来到安塔利亚的代表们带着长长的愿望清单，从让全球经济更多地电气化到为发展中国家提供资金以帮助应对气候变化的影响。笼罩在这一切之上的是，这是第一次正视现实的峰会，即地球将无法实现《巴黎气候协定》的关键目标，升温将比工业化前水平高出 1.5 摄氏度或 2.7 华氏度。联合国表示，要限制这种超调，就需要在未来 10 到 15 年内将化石燃料的使用量减少近一半。许多国家希望达成一项明确呼吁放弃煤炭、石油和天然气的协议。但沙特阿拉伯等产油大国禁止提及化石燃料。最终，欧盟认为没有任何协议比桌面上的协议更好。达拉·奥布莱恩 (Darragh O'Brien) 是爱尔兰环境部长。
达拉·奥布莱恩（DARRAGH O'BRIEN）：我们不会支持甚至不提及化石燃料的封面决定或安塔利亚协议，化石燃料是气候变化的关键驱动因素。
沃尔德霍兹：许多谈判代表拖着行李箱离开会展中心前往机场。他们将于明年在埃塞俄比亚举行的下一届气候峰会上开始谈判。我是来自土耳其安塔利亚的 Rachel Waldholz。
